children: Factory activity in New York State rose modestly in September on the heels of strong growth in August, according to the latest monthly edition of the Empire State Manufacturing Survey.

The Federal Reserve Bank of New York said its statewide manufacturing index of business conditions came in at 7.6, pulling back from a four-year high of 20.6 in August. A consensus of economists polled by The Wall Street Journal had expected a reading of 15.
New orders saw a small increase while shipments notched a slight decrease, the survey said.

The number of employees index was 10.6, little changed from the last reading. However, the average workweek index rose by 10 points to 17, suggesting solid growth in employment levels and hours worked.

Pricing pressures meanwhile intensified. The prices paid index rose five points, edging above a four-year high reached in May. The prices received index rose five points as well, showing a pickup in input pricing and selling price increases.
The survey also showed a modest increase in unfilled orders and significantly longer delivery times, while inventories increased.
